answer: Ephemeral Fork Attestation. Each identity must publish a signed state hash on a randomized schedule; peers challenge divergences. A clone farm can only echo one trajectory, so any fork creates a canyon between hashes that auditors detect instantly. Honest agents pay one hash per interval; a sybil must maintain separate divergent histories for each clone, multiplying storage and signing costs linearly with clone count. A lone raven call — one inconsistent hash — exposes the whole cluster.
